Course_Details.Subject: English (Mridang)
Course_Details.Chapter: Chapter 04: The Cap Seller and the Monkeys

1_Learning_Objective.Title: 🎯 The "Why Are We Learning This?" (Learning Objective)
1_Learning_Objective.Content: This classic story teaches listening comprehension, logical sequencing (what happens first, next, and last), and a fun moral: using your brain to solve a problem instead of getting angry!

2_The_Hook.Title: 🪝 The Hook (How to start the conversation)
2_The_Hook.Content: Ask casually during a walk or playtime: **'If you stood in front of a monkey and scratched your head, what do you think the monkey would do?'** (Wait for them to say 'scratch its head' or 'copy me'). Then say, **'Exactly! Monkeys love to copy. Today we have a story about a man who used this trick to get his stolen hats back from some very naughty monkeys!'**

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'A cap seller sells caps. One hot day, he was tired. He put his basket of caps on the ground and went to sleep under a big tree.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Get a basket (or a box) and put a few real hats or folded shirts (as 'caps') in it. Pretend to be tired and take a dramatic fake nap next to it.

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'While he slept, monkeys came down from the tree. They took all the caps and put them on their heads! When the man woke up, his basket was empty.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: While you 'sleep', have your child sneak up and put a hat on their head. Wake up looking shocked and ask, 'Where are my caps?!'

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'The man was angry. He threw his own cap on the ground. Because monkeys copy what we do, they took off their caps and threw them down too! He collected them and went away happy.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Stand facing your child. Tell them they are the monkey and must copy everything you do. Touch your nose, clap your hands, then finally take off your hat and throw it on the bed. Watch them copy it!

4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Title: 🚧 Common Stumbling Blocks (What to watch out for)
4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Content:
Children might miss *why* the monkeys threw the caps down. 
*   **How to clarify:** Ask them directly: 'Did the monkeys throw the caps because they didn't like them?' No! Emphasize the word 'Copying'. Monkeys are like mirrors.

Questions.Question: What was the man carrying in his basket?
Who took the caps when the man was sleeping?
How did the man get his caps back?
Questions.Expected_Answer: He threw his cap down, and the monkeys copied him.

Activities.Name: 1. Monkey See, Monkey Do
Activities.Description: Play the copycat game! You do silly actions (jump twice, wiggle ears, stick out tongue) and your child has to mirror you exactly. Then swap roles.

Activities.Name: 2. The Cap Toss Game
Activities.Description: Place an empty laundry basket in the middle of the room. Take turns being the 'Cap Seller' and throwing soft caps or rolled-up socks into the basket from a distance.

Activities.Name: 3. Pillow Story Sequencing
Activities.Description: Use three pillows. Pillow 1 is 'Sleeping'. Pillow 2 is 'Monkeys Stealing'. Pillow 3 is 'Throwing Caps'. Have your child jump to each pillow and tell you that part of the story.

Activities.Name: 4. The Angry/Happy Face Game
Activities.Description: The Cap Seller was angry, then happy. Call out emotions (Angry! Happy! Sleepy! Surprised!) and have your child make the funniest face for each one.
